utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Mr. Djurdjic, you have a matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Just some information or notice to the Trial Chamber. We've done what you suggested that we should do regarding the D316 number which was marked MFI, and we forwarded the necessary documents. So I think that now we can proceed and tender this document into evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There's no further difficulty with that, is there, Ms. Kravetz?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would need to consult with Mr. Stamp. I believe that he may want to address this matter. If it's possible, I could provide an answer after the next break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We'll just hold it until you get some instructions. If we could then have the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, the next witness is Dren Caka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, could I mention for counsel that it will be important if the next -- the two witnesses that are listed this week are finished by the end of the session on Wednesday so that I hope that will be in accordance with the progress we're able to make. If you can finish earlier, you may have a holiday.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to point out with regard to that that Mr. Phillipps only arrived today, so he's only going to be available to start his testimony tomorrow because he's currently being proofed. He only flew in this morning to The Hague -- to Amsterdam.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That will mean that you will need -- well, whoever's taking him to be very, very quick tomorrow morning to give Mr. Djurdjic adequate time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we'll take note of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you please read aloud the affirmation that is shown to you now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down. Now Ms. Kravetz has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Could you please state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: My name is Dren, D-r-e-n; last name is C-a-k-a.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Where were you born, Mr. Caka?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I was born in Kosovo, the city of Gjakove.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And when were you born?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I was born December 6th, 1988.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: In 1999, early 1999, where were you living?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I was living in the street called Milosh Giliq, in the city of Gjakove.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honours, I'm having some problems with the transcript on my end. We're trying to set it up.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Do you recall coming to The Hague three years ago and providing testimony before this Tribunal in a case called Milutinovic et al. in relation to events that took place in your town of Gjakove?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Over this past weekend, did you have the opportunity to read the transcript of the testimony that you gave in that case?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Kindly make pauses between question and answer and answer and question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes, I'm being reminded, Mr. Caka, that since we're going to be speaking the same language in court today we need to pause between question and answer to allow the interpreters and court reporters to do their work. And, sir, if today you were asked the same questions that you were asked when you testified three years ago in the Milutinovic case, would you provide the same answers?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honours, I seek to tender the transcript of the previous testimony. This is 65 ter 05150.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01296.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I wish to note also, Your Honours, that in our 92 ter motion for this witness we had listed three photographs that had been marked by the witness during his previous testimony and a diagram that had also been marked by the witness. I propose, instead of having him mark the photographs again, to simply go through his markings and have them explained to the Court during the course of my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Caka, I would like to take you to events that took place in -- on the night of 1st to 2nd April, 1999. Do you recall where you were staying on the night of 1st April, 1999?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yes, I was staying in Lulzim Vejsa's house, which is two houses away from mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And who were you with on that night?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I was with my mother and three of my sisters.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And where exactly in Lulzim Vejsa's house were you staying?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: We were staying in a basement underneath a pool hall. It's a couple steps from the house, but it's detached from the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And in addition to your mother and three sisters, was there anyone else with you in the basement?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yes, there was a total of 20 people; including me, 21.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, just from what you remember, could you tell us who else was in the basement in addition to your mother and three sisters and yourself?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I do not remember everybody's name, but I remember my mom, three sisters, Luli's wife and five of his kids, and then there was Behar -- Behar's family and a wife and two of his kids. There was Lulzim's wife's mother and her sister were there too. And then there was Dushi, and other people as well I just don't remember their names.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Lulzim Vejsa, was that a relative of yours?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yeah, it is a relative of ours, but some -- more of a long relative. It's through my grandma on my dad's side.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And you've referred to a person by the name of Behar. Do you recall what his last name was?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I don't -- I think it's Haxhiavdija, but I'm not too sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Now, why were all these people in addition to your family sleeping in the basement that night?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: We were staying in the basement -- we were told that it was just a safer place in case of any bombings. And it was also underground and it was -- it just felt safe to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And were there any men in this group of 21 people who were in the basement?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I believe there was one.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And approximately how old was that person?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: An older -- I'm saying around 50s and 60s. I'm not too sure. I was young, so I don't remember most of the things.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And was your father with you that night?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: No, he -- he was staying watch, but he wasn't there when the incident happened. They told us that they wouldn't really harm women and children, they were just looking for men, and that's what we believed. They were staying guard. When then when they heard the police, they took off and then there was just us.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You said that "he was staying watch." Where exactly was he that night?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: He was right --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Speakers are kindly reminded not to overlap and to pause between questions and answers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we're going a bit too fast for the interpreters. I'll repeat my question. I was just asking where your father was that night.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: My father was right by the pool hall where they took people -- like, my father, Lulzim, and Behar, they took turns on staying up and watching. So some of them would sleep, some of them would stay up, so I don't know where my father was exactly at the time. He could have been sleeping or he could have been on watch. But the men weren't there when we woke up and we were told to get out.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, you said that you were woken up. Why were you woken up and by whom?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I was woken up by my mother, saying that the police are here, get up, and the rest of the people were waking up their kids. And matter of five minutes after that the door opened and here were the police officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And what happened after the police officers arrived in the basement?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: They told us to get out. One of them spoke Albanian. He said, You guys are with UCK, KLA; you guys are hiding the men. We told them, We're just women and children. No, we're just trying to be safe.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And did you have to leave the basement at that point?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yes, we did. They walked us in a single-file line towards the house. And when we got to the front of the house, one of Lulzim's daughters was going to go ahead and open the door and the police officer kind of shot it down and she, like, got scared and kind of ran off and then we -- they started, like, telling us -- forcing us inside. We went inside. And we took a right which is a room on the right side of the house, right bottom side -- like, when you enter. And then they sat us around and Flaka got up and tried to make tea. The guy pushed her and started firing. Her mother ran out screaming and crying and they started shooting her. And then after that there was Lulzim's wife and daughter and then my mom -- and just started shooting everybody, just started firing everywhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Who was this person that was firing at everyone?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: He was a police officer, and he was the one that came in and he, like, walked us inside. One of them stood outside while this guy walked us in, and then he just started firing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did you recognise any one of these police officers who took you out of the basement?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The speakers are kindly reminded not to overlap. And if the witness would kindly speak into the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: If you could please come a bit closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I thought I recognised one of them, I could be wrong, but I'm pretty sure he was covering his face. It's this police officer that lived in our street, but I couldn't completely see his face to identify -- know it was him, but I think it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And did these policemen wear any sort of uniform?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: They had blue camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And were they armed, apart from the person who was shooting, were the others armed?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you. Now you've referred to a person by the name of Flaka. Can you explain who she was?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Flaka is the first one -- She tried to get up and make tea. She's the first one that they opened fire on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And do you know who she was, what her full name is?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I don't know her full name. It's Tringa's sister, Tringa's sister, and I don't know what her last name is. It's Flaka, but I don't know the last name.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Who was she related to?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: She was related to Tringa, which is Lulzim's wife.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you said that you thought you recognised one of the police officers as someone who lived on your street. Had you seen this person in police uniform -- similar uniform that you saw him that night on other occasions, or was this the first time that you saw him wearing that uniform that you've described?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I have seen him in a uniform lots of times before that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And when you say you have seen him in a uniform, had you seen him wearing the same type of uniform you saw him wearing that night?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to show you some photographs, and we're going to -- there are three different photographs and we're going to go through them one by one.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: If we could please have 05151 up on the screen first.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Do you recognise this photograph, Mr. Caka?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: We see that the photograph has markings. Are these markings that you yourself made?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I would like you to explain to the Judges what these markings mean, and we'll start with the one at the left with the P, if you could tell us what that stands for?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: The P is -- stands for the pool hall, the basement we were staying at.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So in relation to the pool hall, the basement would have been right underneath it, if I understand correctly?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And the H?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: The H is the house that we were taken to after the basement.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Is this where you've just described the shooting took place?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, what does the C stand for?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: C is the house where -- it's the house I lived in, my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And now we see a P-o-l to the right, what does that stand for?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: It stands for the police officer that I believe I recognised.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So that would have been where he lived at the time?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I seek to tender this exhibit as 05151.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01297.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: If we could move to the next photograph, it's 05152.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now we see this is the same photograph with the same markings and there's an additional circle that's been marked underneath the H and a little caret that's there. Are these markings that you made on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And can you explain what the circle under the large H stands for?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: The circle under the H is Behar's car which we had parked right against the door for the door to be shut so it would be harder to open.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And so it was parked on the inside of the house?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And did you notice anything unusual about the car when you went from the basement to the house that's marked H?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: The car was caught on fire, and it was pushed a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And we see underneath that there's a small marking underneath the circle, what does that marking represent?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: That's where the door is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: That's the entrance to the house?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And that's the entrance that you were saying the car was blocking?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I seek to tender this photograph as 05152.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01298.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: If we could now have 05153 up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: While that is coming up, were you injured in the shooting, Mr. Caka?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Where were you injured?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: My right arm.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And once the shooting stopped, what happened? What did you do once the shooting stopped in the house?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I final decided I should get out of there because there was lots of smoke, the house was on fire. So I -- I exited the room, took off my jacket, and laid down in the hallway for about a couple minutes, pretended to be dead there, also just in case they would come back. And then from there I went to Lulzim Vejsa's bedroom. When I went there, the windows were open and I could finally get some actual air. And I stayed there for about -- a good 10, 15 minutes. I'm not too sure. I jumped out of the window, went to the side of the house, and there was this door there. And I looked to the side of the house and I looked there and I saw these three police officers they were smoking and I figured if I went that way it would be a possibility that they would see me and start shooting. So I took steps back and this was a pool hall so there was alcohol served there and they had beer cases, which the cases there were plastic, and I stacked them up and I jumped over a wall going through Dushi's house and then going through to the back which we had made holes in the hall so you wouldn't have to go to my house through, like, the normal street. So I went through there until I got to my house. And once I got to my house, my aunt heard a noise and saw me for a quick second and she, like, took off. And then I was calling for help and then she came back. She's like, Oh, it's you. What happened? I told her everybody's dead. She told me, she's like, Stop it, you've only had a bad dream. I said, No, I really don't think so. Then we went to my house, we entered through the back, which -- like the back room. And when we went there she walked ahead of me and I kind of fainted. And then she came back and said, What's wrong with you? I'm fainting, I'm losing a lot of blood. What don't you get? She said, It's probably just the sleeping pills. And I said, No it's not. And from there they took us, like, through this hallway in my house and they took us close to the bathroom. My grandfather said, What happened? I told them everybody's dead. I didn't know what to say. He's like, No it's not. And I'm like, Well take a look at my arm. They lit a candle and then they looked at -- I was soaking in blood. And they cut my shirt -- my grandfather cut my shirt with a knife and tied my arm and wrapped it somewhat a little bit just till the next morning. And we stayed in my uncle's room in the back of the house until the next morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: May I stop you there, Mr. Caka. We have another photograph up on the screen. We see it has some markings. Did you make those markings?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: We see a line that leaves from the house and then it goes towards the right to another house that you had marked in an earlier photo. Can you tell us what that line represents?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: The whole thing here it's me trying to make my way to my house, and through there it's like a pathway. Then there was holes made where there was firewood in this room that they had. There was holes made behind that, it was kind of hidden. And then the C is where I ran into my aunt. And then the other one right above it, like the C right beside it, there's a little thing, that's where my aunt was. And the one up top is the room that I actually fainted in when she walked in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So the two markings to the right of the C, if I understood correctly, the first one is where your aunt was. And the one above it to the right is where you fainted?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now we also see that there's three dots close to the location that you had marked as the pool hall. What do those three dots represent?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Those three dots represent the three police officers having a cigarette while I was trying to get away.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I seek to tender this photograph, Your Honours. It is 65 ter 05153.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be P01299.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: If we could have 02279 up on the screen. No, that's the wrong document. It's 65 ter 02279. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: We see this is a document called: "Floor Plan of Main Residence of Milosh Giliq Street 157." Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: We see that the document has a number of markings. Are these markings that you made to the document?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I want to go through these markings one by one and just ask you to explain to the Judges what they represent. If we can start at the bottom where we have an a and a B, if you could tell us what that stands for.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: The a and the B are standing for the two police officers that were on the deck before entering the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, we see that there's a line going from B to a circle that's at the entrance of one of the rooms. What does that represent?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: This is the police officer that took us inside the house and -- took us inside. And then that's where he was standing when he did all the shooting.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And number 1, what does that stand for?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Number 1, that's Flaka. She's getting up to make tea and he pushed her and started firing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And numbers 2 and 3?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Number 3, it's her mother running behind the door; and after that she got shot. And then number 2, that's Lulzim Vejsa's wife and daughter.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And what about 4 and 5 which are in the corner?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Four and 5, that's -- that's my sister and Lulzim Vejsa's son.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And 6 and 7 in the other corner?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: My mother and my baby sister.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did your baby sister also get shot?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: No, she didn't. My mother was changing her diaper and she got shot in the back and she fell on top of my baby sister.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And did -- was there anything that happened that made you think that she was still alive when you left the house? I'm talking about your baby sister.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I knew that she was alive because I heard her crying, and I tried to save her, and I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And why is that?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: My mother was a heavier woman, and I was small kid to begin with, and my good arm was -- it was pretty much useless. And I tried and tried and then it got so smokey at a point that if I would have tried any longer I would have been gone with them too.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, you've mentioned twice that there was smoke in the house. Do you know how our why there was smoke, how a fire got started?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: When we entered, the police officer, the letter P started shooting close to the TV -- there was a cabinet there, a closet with clothes, and he shot at it and it just caught on fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. Now we see there -- what appears to be a hallway, two number 9s or an 8 and a 9. What does that represent?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: That's Behar's wife and son.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And the number 10?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Number 10 is Lulzim's mother.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: We see that there's a line going from the room -- from one of the rooms where there are several people, seven of them, and it goes all the way to the back. What does that line represent?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Right by the hallway here?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes, the line that goes --

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: That's where I laid down a little bit for a couple of minutes when -- after I took off my jacket.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And then that same line goes into a next bedroom and then there's an X. What does that represent?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: That represents me in Lulzim Vejsa's house laying down and staying there for 10, 15 minutes to get some air in my system.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And then we see that that line goes out -- out of the house, and then there are some circles at the top of the plan, what are those?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Those are the beer cases.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So is that line -- does that line show the route that you took as you were leaving?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yes, I left and I went to the corner of the house and I looked around the corner and I saw that the three police officers. And then I came back, I stacked the beer cases where that one circle above it is, and I jumped the wall and escaped from there and went home.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And there's three circles to the left of the house. What does that represent?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: The police officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now we see that here on the plan you've indicated ten people and you had told us earlier that in total with yourself you were -- there were 21. What happened to the other ten people that were in the house?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Well, there was more people in the room. Like, I was behind Dushi, myself, and she was a large woman. So that's the only way I survived is because most of the shots that were fired they hit her before they hit me. And it was smokey. I couldn't really see -- by the time when they started firing, I was trying to hide so I wouldn't get shot as well, but one of them caught me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Was there only one shot fired in our direction or were there additional shots fired?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: There was a lot of shots fired towards me, it's just that one of them caught.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honours, I seek to tender this exhibit. It's 02279.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01300.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I would like to now hand a hard copy of Exhibit 02254 to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And, Mr. Caka, this is a collection of uniforms. I would just like you to look through that and see if you find any type of uniforms that resemble the ones that you saw on the night that we have been speaking about that the men that you've described as policemen were wearing.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Photo number 13 and 14, it's roughly around there. It was so long ago, but it was dark blue around the same colour -- I would say more of the photo number 13.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: That, I believe, is on page 8 of the e-court, and it's page 7 of the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And if you can just finish looking through that if you see anything else.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: And I believe it's either photo 9 or photo 11 for the upper body.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: That's on page 7 of e-court, and it's page 6 of the hard copies, photo 11; photo 9 is on page 6 of the e-court and 5 of the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you. You can close that now unless you want to look some more and see if there's anything else. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I seek to tender this exhibit, Your Honours, 02254.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01301.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Caka, you have already told us that you spent the night with your aunt. The following morning, did you receive any medical assistance for the injury that you had sustained in your arm?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Early that morning we got up, my grandfather and my aunt they put me on my grandfather's bicycle and they wrapped a blanket around me. And they were -- we were on our way to the hospital. Before we left, my dad came and then he's like, Go with them and then we're going to go to Albania and I'll meet you there. I'm like, How are you getting there? He said, Well I'm going to be on foot. And I'm like, Am I ever going to see you? He said, Yeah you will. He came and gave me a kiss and then we were on our way to the hospital. On our way to the hospital we ran into a couple police officers and they asked my grandfather, Where are you going? And he's like, To the hospital. They're like, Oh, why? What happened? He said, Oh he just hurt himself playing. And then they were going to see, and he said, Come on, he's just a kid, we've really got to get to the hospital. They were talking to some other people. So they were like, Okay. They just told us, Okay. Just go ahead. Just keep going. Then we went to the hospital. When we got there, there was this Serbian soldier in -- like, like -- not police uniform, like a soldier uniform, the green uniform. And like, he can already see my arm and he's like, What happened? There's no way that we could have lied to him. I -- my grandfather told him, and he's like, I can't believe they would do such a thing. And he actually got me help right away.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And after receiving medical assistance at the hospital, what did you do? Did you return to your aunt's house?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: We went to my other aunt's house. It's not the same aunt that helped me. We went to another aunt's house, and we stayed there for a couple days until one night we thought the police had came there. And then we heard some noise at night and we escaped through the back of the house. And there was a steep hill to another house, and we were going down and my aunt, she broke her leg that night. And then we decided in the morning we should really just get out of there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So did you and your family members leave Djakovica town?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: We left early that morning, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And how did you leave?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Me, my aunt, her husband and daughter, we left in my aunt's husband's car. My grandmother, grandpa, uncle, and aunt, they -- they went by trucks which took people across -- just elder people that couldn't walk, they just took them. And then we were going like the same -- we saw each other on our way like to Kukes, which is Albania, we saw each other here and there. And it took us roughly three or four days to get across the border.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So it took you four days from Djakovica town to get to the border at Kukes?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And before reaching the Albanian border when you were still in -- driving in the car with your relatives, were you stopped at any point or were you allowed to just cross the border freely?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Well, there was an incident that happened before we went to the border, a police officer in the middle of the night was checking cars and he saw my arm was wrapped up and he had asked my aunt's husband what happened. And he's like, Oh, he just hurt himself playing. And the guy asked to unwrap my arm. And he's like, Come on, he's just a kid, he's sleeping, just leave him alone. And nothing -- like, I didn't get woken up, so I guess everything had went okay. We got to the border, which they took everybody's licence plates and information, like, their passports or any identification that they had of Kosovo. As soon as -- like, at the border so that no cars could come back or anything. They just took the information, the registration papers, the licence plate, and everything.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I would now like to play a very short video-clip. This is 02278, if we could have that played.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: If we could stop that. I'm not getting any interpretation. I don't know if anyone else is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note that they don't have any transcript of the video-clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And it's all too fast.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: The transcript was provided earlier this -- last week, I believe, Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, something's gone wrong in the system, Ms. Kravetz. I don't think we can fix it right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I just ask for Your Honour's indulgence. Just one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We have a copy now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Oh, thank you, I see the copy has been provided. If we could start that again, thank you. And my apologies, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: "Go upstairs on the house.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "When we went into the house, the daughter of Lulzim Vejsa was chased by them with an automatic rifle, but they did not harm her. They only shot at the furniture and the house started burning. "Yes, yes, then what happened, how did they kill them? "Then we were made to sit on the couches. "Then they made us sit on the couches. "They killed their grandfather ..."

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I believe we're having a technical problem playing this video.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm being informed by Ms. Pedersen that there was a problem with Sanction this morning here in the courtroom and it hasn't been solved yet. I wonder if the Registrar could play it from her computer, otherwise I'll move on from this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will see.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It's repeating the first part that we already read. [Voiceover] "They killed the father as well -- no, not the father, the grandfather, Flaka's grandfather was killed and her aunt Muni. "Yes, Muni. "No, Muni is alive. "Really? "Yes, he's alive. "How old was Flaka, Flaka Hoxha? "Did you see them killing Flaka, did they shoot her with an automatic rifle? "Yes, with a machine-gun. "Yes, with a machine-gun. They shot her. He saw that. He saw everything. "Did they shoot them in their back? "Yes, they shot them in their head. "How did you escape? "Those policemen were standing on the kitchen door. I walked away. I was lying down, pretending to be dead, and when they left I went into the room. I almost choked from the smoke. "He was near the door. "He lies down on the ground like dead. "By quiet, Dreni, sweetheart, you'll have a sleep soon. Just like that girl. "And they were moved from the door. He ran in another room which was burning. "How long did you stay there in that room? "I think about half an hour. "And then they left the room. "Don't be afraid darling, don't be afraid. "And then he went there. He waited on the -- on that smoke. "He won't do anything wrong to you. "No, I'm afraid. I'm afraid they will hurt me. "No, they will operate. "I'm afraid they will operate on me. "No they are not going to operate on you. Where did you hear of a person having a surgery in a tent, Dreni? "Don't do anything to me with those scissors. "They will only cut the bandage."

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see Mr. Djurdjic on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, we've waited for this to finish. Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Unfortunately, the video does not tally with the audio. It seems that the interpreter is simply reading a text which was translated before. I hope she -- I wish she had interpreted from what she could hear on the video. We only see the one person, which is the witness, and after he utters something then we have interpretation for only half a minute or so. After that it becomes too confusing and one cannot follow.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have the transcript of the video, and I agree with Mr. Djurdjic that the interpretation was not complete because they were only interpreting the Albanian portions and we couldn't hear the English portions. So I will just ask the witness some questions about this video, and we'll tender it with the transcript so the full text is available to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will take that in stages, Ms. Kravetz. By all means, ask the witness about it --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will assess as it goes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Mr. Caka, did you recognise yourself in that video?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Do you know where you were when that was filmed?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I was in a town called Kukes in Albania, and I was in tents they set up, medical tents, for medical treatment and that's where I was at.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And do you remember when approximately this was filmed? I mean how much time after you had crossed over with your family into Albania?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: This was an -- this was filmed and everything happened within a matter of half an hour after I had crossed the border.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So this was filmed immediately after you had crossed the border?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Who is the person that we see next to you? We see a woman speaking to you.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: That is my aunt, the woman that I had seen at the house where I had escaped.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: The person -- your aunt that you referred to earlier who had assisted you after the assistant, the shooting incident, is that the same aunt?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: The same aunt -- not the one that we went to her house to stay before Albania, it's the aunt that -- the night happened on April 1st and 2nd, the one that said that I had had a bad dream.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. And do you know who is filming this?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honours, I seek to tender this video and the corresponding transcript. The video is 02278, and the transcript is 02277.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The problem at the moment is that it is not possible for the Chamber, nor it would appear Mr. Djurdjic, to understand what is being said. You're going to have to give this more attention, Ms. Kravetz, and perhaps come up with a complete transcript of what is English and Albanian translated into English and discuss that with Mr. Djurdjic. He may be able to agree it. If he can't, at some other later time we will have to attempt to have that played again and see whether we can accept the full transcript --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: The transcript that I'm seeking to tender is the full transcript, and it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: But the problem is we can't understand or verify it. Nor can the witness at the moment. The interpreters have attempted to interpret as it's gone on. You say there was also English language being said. I head one or two words in English, but clearly there was much more. There are a number of people speaking, and it's not clear who they are. And there's part of the video which is not to do with this witness at all. So those matters will need to be attended to and then discussed with Mr. Djurdjic, and then if there is not agreement you can raise the matter with us with a view to some further exploration of what can be done and whether or not the video will be received. Mr. Djurdjic, have you followed that, that the Chamber's not happy at the moment to receive the exhibit. It will mark the video for identification, and we've asked Ms. Kravetz to explore some improvement and clarification of the transcript that goes with it. And she will then discuss that with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we agree that this video should be admitted into evidence once we have completed our discussions. All the matters you raised are also issues of the Defence, and I believe after the translation service has done its part then I will believe there will be no problems left with this video. I can tell you out front that under such conditions we are ready to have that admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness is kindly reminded to speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will receive --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- the video with -- as marked for identification, and with it the transcript. Could I indicate I am on the English channel now receiving a translation in another language.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Me too, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Something has been switched the wrong way. We've confused everybody with what's gone on here, Ms. Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will have those marked for identification and then we would leave the question of receiving the video and the transcript until you have been able to look at the difficulties, deal with them as best you can, and discuss it with Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the video and the transcript will be Exhibit P01302 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We apologise for the technical difficulties we're having this afternoon. What we propose to do is request that the witness be -- that the video be subtitled, so that way it's going to be easier to view it and also understand what is being said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That could well be very helpful. Could I suggest that you might explore briefly with the witness whether, apart from his aunt, there were any other members of his family shown in the video.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can certainly do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Mr. Caka, in the video that we just played in court, were there -- did we see any other members of your family there?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: You can kind of see a little bit, but you can't really tell, but you can hear my family -- two of my family members speak.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And who is the person who's speaking English who's interpreting what you're saying? Do you know who that is?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: He's -- that's the medic, the person that ran out to me and carried me in his arms and rushed to get me help.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And who are these other two persons from your family that you can hear in the background?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: My aunt and my other aunt's husband [Realtime transcript read in error "ex-husband"].

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: That's the same man that we saw also in the video briefly that you were speaking about earlier or is this another aunt?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: The husband -- the aunt is the one who helped me from house -- the one that we stayed in her house afterwards. The one that we stayed in the house, that's her husband and my other aunt.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think line 24 it should be "my aunt and --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Her husband.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- the other aunt's husband."

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Rather than her ex-husband.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And just a last question, Mr. Caka. What sort of treatment did you have to undergo do to the injury that you sustained in your arm? What sort of medical treatment were you given for the injury to your arm?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: At the time?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: At the time they just rewrapped it better -- I mean, they put me to sleep, like, as soon as I was in his arms in that video. As soon as that was done, I was pretty much asleep and I don't remember it from there. They kept me sleeping for a long time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And did you have any operation on your arm or any sort of treatment was given to you, medical treatment, because of the gun-shot wound that you had received?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: As far as I remember, no. And after -- they just rewrapped -- and after I don't remember because I was completely asleep. I remember I woke up, then we got rushed to the helicopter. And me and my aunt, the one that had helped me from the house from the beginning, she came in the helicopter with me and we flew out to Tirana, which we went to an actual hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And for how long did you stay at that hospital, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: A couple months, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this stage I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Caka, my name is Veljko Djurdjic and I'm a member of the Defence team for the accused, Vlastimir Djordjevic. And with me today is a member of the team, Ms. Marie O'Leary. Before I put any questions to you, I would like to extend my sympathy, deepest sympathy, because of your loss of your mother and sisters. And I would like to tell you that both Mr. Djordjevic and I condemn such actions and we join you in your pain. And I would just like to put perhaps a few questions to you today so that you can help us to identify the person who actually committed this act. First of all, you said that this person lived two houses from yours, two houses away from yours on the same street; correct?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Having in mind your age, you must be aware, you must know who these persons are, I mean what their last name is, the persons who lived not far from your home?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I do not remember. I just remember, I -- I was somewhat friends with the son at the time, and the son's name was Nemanjo [phoen]. That's the only thing I, pretty much, can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that in one of your statements you said that he was a young man, that he was about 20 years old; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: The police officer?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Oh, he -- it was his son, the one I was playing with. So, that is wrong. He had a son, and he couldn't have been 20 years old.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now could you tell me what the profession of this policeman was before the war? What was -- do you know what he did?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I just know that he was a police officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Caka, two years ago you testified here at this Tribunal and you also provided a written statement. Now, is your memory or recollection better today than it was then or was it better then?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Well, what I remember, he was a police officer. And what people have said, which is what I remember, is him as a police officer. But people had said that he is one of the leaders of the police officers. But that's what other people have said. Me, I just knew him as a police officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This was a general question. I meant in reference to your entire statement and your testimony in the Milutinovic case. So I would ask you if, in view of the fact that you didn't have any changes to make to your -- either to your statement or to your testimony, and that is the reason why I'm asking you whether your recollection is better now or then at that time, the time when you made that statement and testified?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe the witness has already answered that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please carry on, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if only I can get an answer to my question from the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that's what I remember, and that's all I have to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Caka, please listen carefully to what I'm asking you. You testified or you made a statement in the Milutinovic case, and this transcript from the Milutinovic testimony was -- that was adopted into evidence today and that was what Ms. Kravetz asked you about. And you said that you had read that transcript and you didn't have any changes to make to it. Now you have read it and no changes made; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Correct, but when I did -- if I had said that the police officer was a leader, is -- I'm referring to what people have told me. But as a kid, I remember him as a police officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I've already mentioned -- please, we are moving on to a new question. I'm asking you now about the transcript of your testimonies. Now I would like to ask you this: If there are any discrepancies or any differences between what you said today and what you said during the Milutinovic testimony, would you say that your recollection was better while you were testifying in the Milutinovic case three years ago?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, the way really to go about this is first of all to show to the witness any passages you believe are materially different so that he can identify what it is you're saying has changed. If he then has no particular comment about that, you may want to ask him about his memory. But it's really, I think, A, asking him something that's unlikely to produce a satisfactory answer; and B, it's something that's unlikely to help us for you just to put it to him, without first having identified what you say is different about the statement, the transcript, and the evidence today. Would you like to think about that over the break, Mr. Djurdjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. If we can have that break now, and I will prepare those couple of questions that I have left and then we can wrap up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Caka, we've run to the end of our recording tape and have to have a break. A Court Officer will assist you during the break, and we will resume again at 4.00. And we should be then in a position to deal more quickly and clearly with the point that Mr. Djurdjic is now making. So we will see you again at about 4.00.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, while the witness is being brought in, I should indicate that we have no objection to the admission of D316 MFI which is an exhibit my learned colleague referred to at the start of today's session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Oh, that's very good. We can receive as an exhibit the document D316 that was marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Could I please have Exhibit 5150, that is the transcript from the Milutinovic case. And if we could see page 2656 -- or rather, could we see 2654 first.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Caka, would you please read lines 16 through 25 and then going on to the next page, 26 -- 2565, the first three lines.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: From 16 to what again, sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Through 25, the end of the page.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Caka, would you agree with me that you make no mention here of your IDs being taken away from you on the border with Albania?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I did make of it. I've done a lot of interviews, and I did say that that they took my -- not my ID but they took his licence plate and, like, registration paper and his ID. Because I didn't have any papers of my own when I went across.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But there is no mention here of any documents, any registration plates, or anything similar.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I don't know, but I simply remember them taking the licence plate and registration papers and his information.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see page 2656 on the screens, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Lines 15 through 25, would you please read them.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Caka, you crossed the border in a car and it says here that you remained at the border ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Yes. We were in the border for about roughly ten minutes when they were taking his information away. And as soon as I had crossed the border, I was out of the car and a gentleman ran out to me and carried me and got me help.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just another question, Mr. Caka. Listening to what we heard from you here and also reading the transcript, the people who put these questions to you, men or women, they mention the facts of what had happened at the house that night, and that's how they proceeded putting questions to you. How did they know what happened there?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: I do not know. I believe that my aunt and my other aunt's husband had told them -- because all I can remember is somebody carrying me, rushing to the tents, and that's where they got me help. And the gentleman there started talking to me. I don't even quite well remember the conversation that we had, but now -- like, it refreshes my memory seeing it. And after the whole conversation -- after the video you just had seen, I was put to sleep, and I don't remember anything from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That's clear. What I am not clear on is: How is it that some of the facts that only you knew of, how did these other individuals know about these facts, the individuals that we hear speaking here on the video? The reason I'm asking you is that you will not be present at the time when we're actually going to hear the audio-tape. So let's take this step by step. What was the name of your aunt, the aunt that was there in the video with you?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Nimete.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And her last name?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Babalija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I'm not mistaken, you said there was another relative there next to you. What was his name, his first and last name, please.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: First name Selajdin, last name Dulhosi [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me, were they in the car with you when you crossed the border?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Just Selajdin was in the car. The other aunt was in the trucks that had driven people to the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And the young man that we see on the video, is that a person from the hospital or someone who had actually taken you to hospital? There was a dark-haired young man next to you.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: The young man you're speaking of, he's an Albanian from Kosovo. He's -- he went there just to help people out. He kind of did it as a volunteer, didn't want anything from it. He just wanted to help wounded people. And he was the one -- I've never seen him before. He was the one that treated me. And he spoke English, so he asked me questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see Exhibit D002-5109.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Caka, could you please mark the pattern that you saw on the uniform that this policeman was wearing?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: It was between this one and this one, but more this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us, if you could see that, were these people wearing uniforms of the same pattern and same colour or did they wear different pieces of different uniforms combined?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: It was the same uniform, as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The markings made by the witness are red but very small and they're somewhere near the centre of two of the patterns, the one at the right-hand top and the one on the right-hand edge immediately below the top. The second one has two dots. This exhibit will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00360.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, and I believe it -- just for the sake of clarification of the transcript, at line 37 -- page 37, line 4, the witness indicated "but more this one" and then he made a second dot, marking, at the second photograph to the right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Just one more question, Mr. Caka. What does AK-47 stand for?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: A machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: How come you know that?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Because I'm not a kid and I'm -- anymore, and I've seen a lot of movies, and I know what it's called.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you watch those movies in 1999 perhaps? And since when do you know that the AK-47 is a weapon? I can explain. I found this in your 1999 and 2000 statement, that's why I'm asking you about this. You now say it's an automatic rifle, but in the statement it literally says "AK-47." That's why I'm curious about it.

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: If you go back to my video, I believe I'm saying "machine-gun," which I did not know at the time as an AK-47. But I had described to people what it looked like and they had gone -- like, they went from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Caka. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djurdjic. Ms. Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I just want to clarify two matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You were asked by my learned colleague about what happened at the border when you crossed and you said in response to one of his questions that they took his licence plates and registration papers and his ID. Who were you referring to when you said they took his licence plates?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: Selajdin, my other aunt's husband.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And who is it who took his licence plates and his ID card?

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: The police at the border.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you. Now you were also asked about the name of your aunt and you gave the name Nimete. Which of your two aunts is this one? Is this the one to whose house you went right after the incident occurred, or is this the aunt you saw later, the next day I believe or --

utterances.speaker: DREN CAKA
utterances.text: This -- Nimete is the aunt that helped me that -- when I went from Luli Vejsa's house to my house. That's Nimete.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't know if this will assist the Court, but Ms. Pedersen has just informed me that we can now play the full video with audio. We can play it again if it will be of assistance to the Chamber, if not we can simply get a new copy with subtitles as I had indicated. It's just since the witness is here and if there are any questions from the Chamber. I thought --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It might be a precaution to play it again while the witness is here, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Well, we will try again, and I hope we have better luck this time with our technology.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: "Go to them, go upstairs on the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "This girl here was shot with automatic rifle and then they started to burn the house. "And then how did they kill them? "They entered into the basement then they started to shoot. "Okay. Okay. "They killed also his father -- his grandfather, in fact, not his father. And his -- Muni, Muni is alive. And then they set fire to the house --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The voices are indistinct. [Voiceover] "And then they killed the old woman with an automatic rifle. "He saw that. He saw that. "How did they shoot them? Behind the back? They shot them at the back? "They shot them one by one. They were shot on the back one by one, not all of them. "How did they kill them? "They were those policemen. I was walking slowly, and I pretended I was dead. When they left, I went to the room." This guy is repeating the words of the little boy. [Voiceover] "When they moved from the door he said he ran in the direction of another room. There was lot of smoke. He stayed there. "How long did you stay there, dear? "I think half an hour. "And then what did you do? "And then they left. "I'm afraid. I'm afraid. "Don't be afraid, dear. He waited in that atmosphere full of smoke. "Don't do anything to my hand. "No, no, we won't do anything. "Explain to him that I'm going to do something to his arm. "They will bandage the arm. "Please don't make an operation on me. "No, no, they won't operate on you. They won't operate on you. No, no, they won't. They don't do anything wrong to you. "When did they shoot?"

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions for the witness. We will at another stage seek to tender a subtitled version just so that everything that is said is recorded adequately. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Caka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is there anything arising from that re-playing that you want to pursue further, Mr. Djurdjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The translation we heard now differs from the translation we received together with the exhibit, which is 2277 on the 65 ter list. Once we receive the transcript of what is actually said, we will not object any longer to this piece of evidence being admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, yes, thank you for that. We will await the full subtitled video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Caka, you'll be pleased to know that that concludes the evidence and the questions that will be asked of you. The Chamber has the transcript of the evidence you gave last time and, of course, what you have said today. We want to thank you for coming once again to The Hague and for the assistance that you've been able to give us today, and you may, of course, now return to your normal activities.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Court Officer will show you out when we rise. So thank you again and I hope life goes well with you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is there any other matter that should detain us at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I just have one matter. It's unrelated to the testimony of this witness, so if the witness could be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness could go now --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- and we'll deal with that matter. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honours, just an administrative matter. It concerns Exhibit P1029, which is a selection of pages of the Blue Book which we tendered during the testimony of General Drewienkiewicz. I believe on 26 June it was admitted by the Chamber. It has just been brought to my attention that the version that is currently in e-court has a problem with the pagination of pages, they're not in chronological order and this makes it rather difficult to review the exhibit. So we would like to seek leave of the Chamber to replace the version that's in e-court, both the English and B/C/S versions of this exhibit, for a new revised version that's in correct order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Prosecution will have leave to substitute a correctly paginated version of Exhibit P1029.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And as I indicated at the start of the session, we have no further witnesses for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very good. Well, we will look forward then to a prompt handling of the witness tomorrow and the next day, if necessary. We will now adjourn and resume tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 1st day of September, 2009, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.27 p.m.,
